A: Are the observed resolved-subset market/community frozen Brier means in ForecastBench 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-11 informative about their full 250-market-question cohorts when binary outcomes are missing, without unverifiable MCAR/ignorability assumptions?

B.H1: Worst-case missing binary outcomes bound the full-cohort Brier broadly; at least one cohort's interval contains the illustrative p=.5 Brier .25. Resolved-only market Brier is not transferable to all events.
B.H0: Both full-cohort upper bounds are <.25, meaning even arbitrary missing binary outcomes cannot overcome the weak p=.5 threshold; this would still not prove competence vs strong forecasting baselines.
rivals: Publication/readiness selection may give nonignorable censored outcomes.
External frozen market p is not PFL participant predictions, proper benchmark is the original platform methods or an independent competitive baseline; p=.5 is not competent.
B.falsifier: If all outcomes uniquely resolved and all records p valid, lower=upper=observed mean, contrary to wide missingness.

C.original_source: ForecastBench ICLR 2025 original official CC BY-SA 4.0 public question and resolution sets
C.method: For every valid market question frozen probability p in [0,1] before due, if exactly one observed binary y with resolution date after due and strictly before as_of=2026-10-29, loss=(p-y)^2. If y unknown, min loss=min(p^2,(1-p)^2), max loss=max(p^2,(1-p)^2). Sum all over eligible public market questions and divide by eligible count; no imputation, distribution, sampling or statistical CI.
C.risk_set: market sources allowlist kalshi/manifold/metaculus/polymarket, duplicate source+id fails, missing/invalid numeric p excluded and counted, other raw quantity sources excluded
C.primary_outcome: lower/upper bound of mean Brier for full market-question cohort at as_of=2026-10-29; known/unknown counts, known resolved-only mean separate
C.illustrative_reference: 0.25 for p=.5, explicitly a weak diagnostic not competent predictive comparator
